verses.text: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:
Who is this, clouding my counsel with words spoken without knowledge?
Brace yourself like a man. I’ll ask the questions, and you’ll answer me.
Where were you when I laid the earth’s foundations? Tell me, if you understand.
Who set its dimensions, if you know? Who stretched a measuring line across it?
What holds its foundations in place? Who set its cornerstone
while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Who shut the sea behind doors when it burst out of the womb,
when I dressed it in clouds and wrapped it in thick darkness,
when I marked its boundary and put doors and bars in place,
and said, ‘You can come this far and no farther. This is where your proud waves stop’?
Have you ever given orders to the morning or shown the dawn where to rise,
so it could grab the earth by its edges and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth takes shape like clay beneath a seal, and its features stand out like folds in a garment.
The wicked lose their light, and their raised arm is broken.
Have you gone down to the springs of the sea or walked through the hidden depths?
Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of death’s shadow?
Have you taken in the full width of the earth? Tell me if you know all of it.
Which way leads to where light lives? And where does darkness live,
so you could take each one home and find the paths to where they belong?
Of course you know! You were already born back then, and you’ve lived for so many years!
Have you entered the storehouses of snow or seen where I keep the hail,
which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of battle and war?
Which way does lightning spread, and how does the east wind scatter over the earth?
Who dug a channel for the floodwaters and made a path for thunderstorms,
to send rain on land where no one lives, on wilderness with no people,
to soak the empty wasteland and make new grass sprout?
Does rain have a father? Who fathers the drops of dew?
From whose womb did ice come? Who gave birth to the gray frost from the sky?
Water turns hard as stone when the surface of the deep freezes over.
Can you tie the stars of the Pleiades together or untie Orion’s cords?
Can you bring the constellations out in their seasons or guide the Bear with her cubs?
Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you make those laws govern the earth?
Can you call up to the clouds so a flood of water comes down over you?
Can you send lightning on its way? Does it report back to you, ‘Here we are’?
Who put wisdom deep inside people? Who gave the mind understanding?
Who is wise enough to count the clouds or tip over the water jars of the sky,
when the dust packs together and the lumps of earth stick to one another?
Can you hunt for the lioness or feed her hungry young
when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the brush?
Who finds food for the ravens when their young cry out to God and wander because they have nothing to eat?
